inputs.text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are being asked to trust government promises while their jobs remain without legal protection. Their protest outside the Presidential Palace and 24-hour strike make clear who carries the risk when commitments are unenforceable: workers, not officials. If the government says it has met their main demands, it should prove it by putting job security in binding guarantees. Precarious work is a power imbalance, and workers’ rights should never rest on trust alone.
